text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout 'model-v2b/rolling-update' in us-west-2 showing anomalous outputs and token errors. Metric: 12% invalid tokens, 18% client-reported hallucinations over last 10m. Affected artifact: weightset-2026-03-17-v2b. Severity: SEV2. Paging @oncall-ml and @oncall-sre.
ben (oncall-ml): ack, looking. Can you dump recent canary request/response samples and the tokenizer mismatch logs? Linking logs would help.
frank (oncall-sre): oncall-sre here. If this is causing customer-visible bad outputs, we should stop the rollout and flip the rollout flag. Dan — can you confirm kill-switch path?
dan (release): I see the rollout controller still at 60% traffic. Command to flip (internal): `/rollout kill --id model-v2b-2026-03-17 --reason "canary-invalid-tokens"` — I'll run once we agree. ETA <2m.
carla (product): Heads-up — we have increased error reports from the webchat surface; this might hit a few mid-market customers. Product suggests immediate stop.
eleine (cs): ACME and BrightLayer reported noisy responses 5m ago. I'm prepping an outbound note. Please tag affected customers in the final incident summary.
ben (oncall-ml): quick look at canary logs: tokenizer warnings: `Tokenizer.decode(): unknown id 50256, replacement char used` and `KV cache mismatch` noise. Also noticing weights file header `quantized: false` while deploy manifest expected `quantized: int8`. Possible mismatch between build and release metadata.
frank (oncall-sre): agree stop-first. Dan please execute kill, then we'll roll back to model-v2a-stable.
dan (release): executing now `/rollout kill --id model-v2b-2026-03-17 --reason "canary-invalid-tokens"`
deploy-bot: Rollout controller acknowledged. Killing rollout id model-v2b-2026-03-17. Previous traffic: 60%. New traffic: 0%. Actions: auto-redirect to fallback model-v2a-stable. (run_id: dpl-2026-03-17-0812)
frank (oncall-sre): :thumbsup: traffic redirected, health checks green on fallback. Confirming no new client errors in the last 30s.
ben (oncall-ml): pulling the artifact — hash mismatch between artifact registry and release manifest. It looks like build pipeline published a non-quantized weightset but release manifest references quantized variant. I suspect a tag mismatch in the CI step that picks the artifact.
carla (product): any immediate customer-impact classification? SEV2 -> call with CS if ACME impacted?
elaine (cs): contacting ACME now, will escalate to account exec. Preparing a short note: "We paused a canary due to model outputs; no data exfiltration, fallback to stable model. We'll follow up with details." ETA 10m.
ben (oncall-ml): quick mitigation checklist: 1) keep rollout killed 2) block any subsequent releases that reference the bad artifact tag 3) create a hotfix job to rebuild and verify quantization metadata before re-release 4) run regression prompts against canary samples.
frank (oncall-sre): adding a temporary repo rule to prevent the bad tag from being promoted: `repo:disallow:promote:weightset-2026-03-17` until QA completes.
dan (release): opening a post-release investigation ticket: INC-444460-KG. Will include CI pipeline logs. Assigning to @ben and @release-ci.
ben (oncall-ml): initial root-cause hypothesis: CI step `pack_weights` did not pick `--quantize int8` flag for the v2b builder variant; manifest still pointed to quantized path. That leaves tokenizer expecting different token offsets. Repro locally with sample payloads.
frank (oncall-sre): good to know. For now mark incident state: mitigated (traffic routed to stable), monitoring. We'll keep the page active until postmortem ticket created.
carla (product): please capture customer-facing timeline and action items. We'll schedule an incident review tomorrow.
elaine (cs): ACME responded: "Thanks for the quick action, please keep us posted." I sent a follow-up note linking to fallback assurance and ETA for root cause.
deploy-bot: Automated snapshot of canary logs saved to s3://redwood-incidents/4444601234/canary-logs.tar.gz
ben (oncall-ml): saving sample mismatched outputs to the ticket. Next steps: reproduce, rebuild with quantize flag, run smoke evals, then small canary with strict token sanity checks.
frank (oncall-sre): leaving oncall watch for 30m. If any regressions, escalate to SEV1.
incident-bot: Incident state updated: MITIGATED. Owner: dan (release). Postmortem ticket: INC-444460-KG. Participants: ben, frank, carla, elaine, dan, deploy-bot.
